# PR #2839: Patch: the fuzz gate probes playing through an open prompt

Closes #2829

## What changed and why

The fuzz gate forged reused nonces, wrong seats, and malformed answers/actions, but never the simplest illegal move: playing a card or ending the turn while a prompt is open (§9.3, R79). Two files changed, no engine rule touched:

- [invariants.rs](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-2829/crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs): new `PROMPT_OPEN_PLAY_ACTION` / `PROMPT_OPEN_END_TURN_ACTION` constants and `prompt_blocked_action(state, player)`, next to `malformed_actions`. It returns `None` with no prompt open or a mulligan one (R265–R266 path untouched); otherwise a `Play` naming the seat's first held card, or `EndTurn` when the hand is empty.
- [fuzz.rs](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-2829/crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs): new `PROMPT_OPEN_PROBE` and a block in `probe_state` (between the malformed-answer and malformed-action loops) that forges that action with a fresh nonce through the existing `judge_probe` machinery, owed a refusal with no events and a byte-identical state. Stride and budget constants are byte-identical.

Two tests in `mod fuzz_probe_stage`: a refusal test driving real games (seeds 2–20) to an open non-mulligan prompt, forging both `Play` and `EndTurn` and asserting refusal, empty events, identical state, plus `probe_state(...) == None` with the real reducer; and a tripwire test with a reducer that accepts forged `Play`/`EndTurn` under an open prompt, asserting the gate fails naming the `prompt-open` probe and its step.

## How tested

- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools fuzz_probe_stage`: 9 passed, 0 failed (7 existing + 2 new).
- `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit invariants`: green.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh` (full binary suite): 462 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored (dailies).
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean (one reformat of the new test applied via `cargo fmt`).
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` and same for `jackioh-engine`: clean.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: ok (1625 rulings, 3848 proofs).
- `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200`: 200 passed, 0 failed, 0 failed a probe. Same for `--handicap`. Duos fuzz untouched (`duos_fuzz.rs` never calls `probe_state`).

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- Forged seat is the seat to act, which equals the prompt holder whenever a prompt is open; I rejected forging from the opponent's seat because the wrong-seat probe already covers that axis.
- Never forge `Concede` or `SetAutoEndTurn`: R211/R345 allow them while prompted, so forging them would be probe noise. Rejected `OfferDraw`/`Emote` for the same reason (allowed types per `PROMPT_OPEN_ACTION_TYPES`).
- No new ruling: the refusal is already specified (§9.3, R79), so this only probes it; comments cite R79/R265/R266 and `spec check` passes.
- Followed the planner's plan exactly; no departures.

Worth a second look: the refusal test's game-driving loop answers mulligans via `seat_to_act` rather than the gate's `actor_of` mulligan ordering — both orders reach prompts, and the loop tries seeds 2–20 until one opens a non-mulligan prompt, so this is robust to deck/pool drift but would `panic!` loudly if no seed ever prompts.

# #2829: Patch: the fuzz gate probes playing through an open prompt
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The fuzz gate plays thousands of random games and also sends forged illegal actions to make sure the engine refuses them with the game untouched. Today it never tries the simplest illegal move of all: playing a card, or ending the turn, while a question is still open. After this change it does, so an engine slip that accepts such a move fails loudly at the exact step.
## Why
While a prompt is open the engine refuses everything but its answer and game-ending actions (`reduce.rs`: a prompt blocks every action but its own answer and the ones that end a game, §9.3, R79; BUILD M1-T3). But `probe_state` in `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` only forges a reused nonce, a wrong seat, malformed answers and malformed actions, and `malformed_actions` in `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs` only forges variants of a Play choice, so when a prompt is open (the chosen action is an Answer) no non-answer probe is ever sent. Invariants I7 (orphaned work) and I10 (opponent-held prompts) do not check this refusal either.
## Proposal
Add one probe to `probe_state`: while a non-mulligan prompt is open, forge the seat's non-answer action (a Play when its hand holds one, else EndTurn) with a fresh nonce, owed a refusal with no events and an unchanged state, through the existing `judge_probe` machinery. Reuse `malformed_actions` shapes where they fit; keep the mulligan path (R265-R266) exactly as it is.
## Where it lands
Files: `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` (`probe_state`, probe stride unchanged), `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs` (`malformed_actions` and neighbors). SPEC sections: §10.6 (prompts), §9.3 and R79 (prompt blocks), R265 (mulligan).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New tools unit test: a forged Play during an open prompt is refused, with no events and a byte-identical state; same for EndTurn.
- [ ] The fuzz gate (`fuzz --seeds 200` at least) and the handicapped wave stay green; Duos fuzz is untouched.
- [ ] No new numbers: stride and budget constants unchanged (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
## Size and risks
Small to medium work, suggested `difficulty:medium` (test tooling plus a testkit helper, no engine rule change). Risk is probe noise on exotic prompts; the owed-refusal contract (`judge_probe`) is already the standard all other probes meet.

   ```rust
   if let Some((variant, seat, body)) = prompt_blocked_action(state, player) {
       let forged = Action::new(body, seat, format!("fuzz-probe-{step}"));
       if let Some(wrong) = judge_probe(state, &probe(state, &forged), None) {
           return Some(format!(
               "{PROMPT_OPEN_PROBE} probe after step {step}: {seat} sent the {variant} while a prompt was open, and it {wrong}"
           ));
       }
   }
   ```

Then: assert `prompt_blocked_action` returns `Some` with the play variant iff the holder's hand is non-empty, else the end-turn variant; forge **both** a `Play` (holder's first hand card id, or the literal `"prompt-open-probe-no-card"` when the hand is empty — the prompt gate refuses either) and `EndTurn` from the holder with fresh nonces through `reduce`; assert each has `error.is_some()`, empty events, `result.state == state`, and `judge_probe(&state, &result, None).is_none()`. Finally assert `probe_state(&state, player, &chosen, last, step, reduce).is_none()`, proving the real engine passes the extended gate at that step. (All names used — `register_all`, `preview_every_set`, `decks_for_seed`, `Rng`, `seat_to_act`, `subsystems::choose_action`, `CreateGameOptions`, `create_game`, `begin_game`, `reduce`, `judge_probe`, `probe_state`, `Action`, `ActionBody`, `PromptKind` via `jackioh_engine::PromptKind` — are already imported or one qualified path away.)
5. Add the tripwire test in the same module: a reducer that only diverts forged probe actions and lets the real game play identically:
   ```rust
   fn takes_prompt_open_plays(state: &GameState, action: &Action) -> ReduceResult {
       if state.pending.as_ref().is_some_and(|pending| pending.kind != jackioh_engine::PromptKind::Mulligan)
           && matches!(action.body, ActionBody::Play { .. } | ActionBody::EndTurn)
           && action.nonce.starts_with("fuzz-probe-")
       {
           return ReduceResult { state: state.clone(), events: Vec::new(), error: None };
       }
       reduce(state, action)
   }
   #[test]
   fn a_reducer_that_accepts_a_play_while_a_prompt_is_open_fails_the_prompt_open_probe() {
       assert_caught_at(2, takes_prompt_open_plays, PROMPT_OPEN_PROBE);
   }
   ```
   (Seed 2 opens a prompt; the existing malformed-answer test already relies on this.) This proves an engine slip fails loudly at the exact step.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools fuzz_probe_stage` — runs the two new tests plus all existing probe tests (wrong-seat, reused-nonce, malformed-answer/action, mulligan, judge).
- `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit invariants` — compiles and checks the touched testkit file.

- [ ] Forged `Play` during an open prompt refused, no events, identical state; same for `EndTurn` (new tools test green).
- [ ] Slip-accepting reducer fails the `prompt-open` probe naming its step (tripwire test green).
- [ ] Existing probe/mulligan/judge tests, `fuzz --seeds 200`, and 200 handicapped seeds green; stride and budget constants byte-identical.
- [ ] `fmt --check`, both crates' clippy, and `spec check` green; no spec, catalog, or web file touched.

## Risks

- Probe noise on exotic prompts: impossible by construction — `reduce.rs` refuses `Play`/`EndTurn` before any prompt-specific logic while `pending` is open, and game-ending actions (`Concede`, server actions) plus `SetAutoEndTurn` are never forged. - Empty-hand holder: falls back to `EndTurn`, still a refused non-answer action; the test forges both bodies regardless.
- Mulligan regression: helper returns `None` unless `pending` holds a non-mulligan prompt; the mulligan test (`a_mulligan_keeping_an_undealt_card…`) pins the old path.

None.
